text:
Richard Stallman is a prominent computer scientist and the founder of the Free Software Movement, best known for creating the GNU operating system and the Linux distribution. Born in 1953, he studied physics at Harvard and MIT before dedicating his career to software freedom. Stallman advocates for the philosophical stance that software should be free, meaning users have the freedom to study, modify, and redistribute it, distinguishing "free software" from "open source" by emphasizing liberty over convenience. He established the Free Software Foundation (FSF) in 1985 and popularized the concept of "copyleft" through the GNU General Public License (GPL) to ensure software remains free even when derived from proprietary code.
Stallman has been a vocal activist against proprietary software, digital rights management, and software patents, engaging in public protests and campaigns to protect user privacy and freedom. He has faced significant personal and professional challenges, including controversy surrounding his comments on the Jeffrey Epstein case in 2019, which led to his resignation from MIT and the FSF in 2019. Despite this, he returned to the FSF board in 2021 after public debate. Stallman is known for his uncompromising commitment to his principles, his specific terminology regarding software freedom, and his use of free software in his personal life, including his computer and communication methods, to resist surveillance.
